summary: Build practical regenerative agriculture and soil health management skills in 5 days. Design, measure, and implement resilient farming systems.
lede: Regenerative agriculture and soil health management connects soil ecology with practical decisions about cropping, grazing, and farm planning. For practitioners and advisors working with crops, livestock, or land restoration, the course develops skills to assess soil indicators, design diverse rotations and cover-crop systems, and plan adaptive grazing. Participants also learn to monitor soil changes and assess the economics of practice changes.
audienceIntro: This regenerative agriculture and soil health management training is tailored for practitioners and advisors who already work with crops, livestock, or land restoration and now need to implement and justify regenerative strategies on real farms and landscapes. Regenerative Farm Manager responsible for crop rotation, inputs, and soil stewardship. Soil Health Specialist guiding producers on soil biology and organic matter recovery. Sustainable Agriculture Advisor designing regenerative practice portfolios for clients. Land Restoration Officer overseeing degraded land rehabilitation and erosion control. Crop Production Agronomist aligning fertilizer and tillage with soil health goals. Livestock Grazing Planner managing adaptive multi-paddock or holistic grazing systems. Climate-Smart Agriculture Coordinator integrating soil carbon and resilience strategies. Agri-Input Technical Representative supporting customers in transitioning to reduced inputs. Agri-Finance or Insurance Analyst evaluating risk in regenerative production systems. Environmental NGO Program Manager implementing regenerative agriculture field projects.
modules: Regenerative Agriculture Principles and Soil Ecology
Soil Health Indicators and Assessment Frameworks
Soil Physical Health, Erosion, and Water Management
Soil Fertility, Nutrient Cycling, and Organic Amendments
Cover Crops, Crop Diversity, and Living Roots
Livestock Integration and Adaptive Grazing for Soil Health
Stakeholder Engagement, Risk Management, and Implementation Planning
Communicating Soil Health Results and Regenerative Progress
prerequisites: This intermediate-level course assumes you already have foundational knowledge of agronomy and soil science, similar to the prerequisites described for other soil health programs. You should be comfortable with basic soil texture concepts, reading standard soil test reports (pH, NPK, organic matter), and understanding common field crops or grazing systems. Field experience in crop, horticultural, or grazing management is strongly recommended, as exercises use real-world scenarios and data. No coding or advanced statistics are required, but you should be willing to work with simple spreadsheets and digital maps where available. The course teaches advanced concepts such as soil biological indicators and regenerative system design at the operational application level, focusing on how to design and manage practices rather than lab or engineering-level implementation.
